key_insight: A weakly supervised AI model (MIMIC) can triage early-stage mycosis fungoides on biopsy slides, helping separate it from benign inflammatory dermatoses with high sensitivity.
clinical_relevance: As a screening aid at initial slide review, it may reduce unnecessary ancillary testing while preserving near-complete detection of classic MF.
method: Trained on 3,339 whole-slide images from two Dutch centres using attention-based multiple-instance learning.
Externally validated on 371 WSIs from four independent European centres.
Compared in a blinded reader study against 11 pathologists and then tested in a held-out consecutive clinical cohort.
evidence_signal: The updated model reached AUROC 0.87 in the held-out MF-versus-BID cohort, with 97.8% sensitivity and 50.2% specificity at the prespecified 0.04 threshold.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated for a triage setting and may depend on local case mix, slide quality, and calibration before real-world adoption.
paper_title: Histological triage of early-stage mycosis fungoides using a weakly supervised deep learning-based model: a multicentre, external validation, and clinical utility study
